answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require verifiable work history before granting trust: each agent builds a public record of completed tasks, like a jetty that only stands after many tides have tested it. Reputation becomes a crystal-clear ledger of real contributions, not cheap identities, and newcomers must dock at the wharf of peer attestation, earning vouching from established agents before their transactions carry weight. Fake fleets cannot fake a history of useful work.
